description:
Snehasanthwanam is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Kerala. 

It was launched in the year 2020. 

The primary aim of the scheme is to provide support and assistance to children who have lost their parents due to the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The scheme is designed to ensure that these children receive adequate care and protection. 

The Government of Kerala recognized the urgent need for such a scheme in the wake of the pandemic. 

The scheme was officially launched on June 1, 2021. 

The objectives of Snehasanthwanam include providing financial assistance to orphaned children. 

The scheme also aims to facilitate educational support for these children. 

Another objective is to ensure emotional and psychological support for the affected children. 

The government has set a target to cover all children who have lost their parents due to COVID-19. 

The scheme aims to provide assistance to at least 1,000 children in its initial phase. 

The benefits under the scheme include a monthly financial assistance of ₹3,000. 

This financial assistance is provided until the child reaches the age of 18 years. 

In addition to financial support, the scheme also includes provisions for educational assistance. 

Children will receive support for school fees and other educational expenses. 

The scheme also provides for health insurance coverage for the children. 

The health insurance will cover medical expenses up to ₹5 lakh. 

This is crucial for ensuring the well-being of the children. 

Eligibility for the Snehasanthwanam scheme is specifically defined. 

Children who have lost one or both parents due to COVID-19 are eligible. 

There is no age limit for eligibility as long as the child is under 18 years. 

The scheme is open to all children irrespective of their socio-economic background. 

There are no specific income criteria for the families of these children. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must fill out a registration form available online. 

The form can be accessed through the official Kerala government website. 

Applicants must provide proof of the child's age and the death certificate of the parent(s). 

Additional documents may include proof of residence and identity. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local authorities. 

The local child welfare committee plays a crucial role in the approval process. 

The timeline for processing applications is typically within 30 days. 

Once approved, the financial assistance is disbursed monthly. 

The first disbursement is made within a week of approval. 

Subsequent payments are made on the first of every month. 

The implementing authority for the Snehasanthwanam scheme is the Department of Social Justice, Kerala. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the implementation and monitoring of the scheme. 

Local bodies such as Gram Panchayats and Municipalities are also involved in the execution. 

They assist in identifying eligible children and facilitating the application process. 

The scheme has been well-received by the public and has garnered significant attention. 

As of October 2023, over 1,500 children have benefited from the scheme. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹50 crore for the initial phase of the scheme. 

This budget is aimed at providing financial assistance and support services. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of mental health support. 

Counseling services are made available to help children cope with their loss. 

The government collaborates with NGOs and local organizations for effective implementation. 

These organizations provide additional support services such as mentorship and guidance. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Kerala government to support vulnerable populations. 

It aligns with the state's commitment to child welfare and protection. 

The government has also launched awareness programs to inform the public about the scheme. 

These programs aim to reach out to those who may not be aware of the available support. 

The success of the Snehasanthwanam scheme is monitored through regular assessments. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the services offered. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's proactive approach in times of crisis. 

It highlights the importance of community support in addressing social issues. 

The Kerala government continues to evaluate and expand the scheme based on needs. 

Future plans may include extending benefits to children affected by other crises. 

The overall goal is to create a safety net for children in distressing situations. 

The scheme is a crucial step in ensuring that no child is left behind. 

It reflects the government's commitment to social justice and equity. 

The implementation of Snehasanthwanam is a collaborative effort. 

It involves various stakeholders including government departments and civil society. 

The scheme has set a precedent for similar initiatives in other states. 

It serves as a model for addressing the needs of orphaned children. 

The government remains dedicated to enhancing the welfare of its citizens. 

The Snehasanthwanam scheme is a significant part of this commitment. 

It aims to empower children and provide them with a brighter future. 

The scheme is expected to evolve as new challenges arise. 

Continuous support and adaptation will be key to its success. 

The government encourages families and communities to engage with the scheme. 

This engagement is vital for ensuring that all eligible children receive assistance. 

The Snehasanthwanam scheme stands as a beacon of hope for many. 

It embodies the spirit of resilience and solidarity in the face of adversity. 

Through this initiative, the Kerala government aims to build a stronger society. 

The focus remains on nurturing and protecting the most vulnerable members of the community. 

The scheme is an essential part of Kerala's welfare landscape. 

It represents a commitment to the future of the state's children. 

The government continues to seek innovative solutions to support its citizens. 

The Snehasanthwanam scheme is an important step in this ongoing journey.
